newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - steady to narrowly weaker.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - steady to narrowly weaker.

text.p: Med oil products were steady or a touch easier on Wednesday.
Large gas oil cargoes of up to 60,000 tonnes were still able to attract stronger premiums against smaller parcels because of their flexibility to be shifted out of the region.
Heating oil cargoes of an arbitrage size were assessed at fob high quotes +$3, about $1 down on Tuesday's levels with smaller cargoes at fob high quotes +$1, broadly unchanged.
Although more talk has developed about shipping material eastwards, so far only a couple of cargoes have been done out of region and their destination is northern Europe, traders said.
High sulphur fuel oil was around a dollar weaker amid good supplies out of the Black Sea and from mideastern sellers.

Dealers said a trader used 40,000 tonnes of Isab material for a 70,000 tonne Romanian tender, and was paid $4.50 under the quoted cif mean. A trader was heard to be bringing 100,000 tonnes of Arabian high sulphur straight-run fuel, partly from Rabigh, to the Med. At least part of the cargo was expected to move to be refined in Greece.
Low sulphur fuel was weaker, and March swaps traded as low as $98.50 fob NWE before recovering by around a dollar.
A trader with a commitment into a Turkish tender was heard to have fixed 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil from the Caribbean to cover the requirement.
Gasoline held steady, continuing to focus on the lack of cargoes for Feb and some demand from Africa and the U.S.
The arbitrage to the U.S. was seen as shut but prices were still expected to hold steady for the rest of February.

Naphtha was quiet, with prices tagging along to the strong NWE market where prompt demand was buoying cargoes. One trader said an end-user in NWE and Brazil's Petrobras had each bought 250,000 tonnes of naphtha this month, tightening supply.
